content.intro: This lesson belongs to Module 12: Database and Server-Side Injection Vulnerabilities. It builds practical understanding of XML External Entity and XML Security with the syllabus subtopics retained below.
content.why_it_matters: XML External Entity and XML Security addresses how untrusted data or requests cross a boundary and may influence application behavior. The safe fix should address the root cause and remain testable. Treat external input and identity claims as untrusted until validated, enforce the control on the server, and cover expected and denied behavior with regression tests.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: XML External Entity and XML Security can be understood through this sequence: Receive untrusted data → Keep data separate → Validate safe interface → Regression test. Start with the application asset and trust boundary, state what secure behavior should occur, and identify the evidence that would prove or disprove it.

content_blocks.title: Connect the syllabus subtopics
content_blocks.text: The source curriculum groups this lesson around: 91.1 XML parsing and document type declarations; 91.2 External entity processing risks; 91.3 File and network access implications; 91.4 Secure parser configurations; 91.5 XML schema and data validation; 91.6 Safer alternatives for data interchange. Treat these points as a checklist, not a list to memorize: explain the risk, identify the root cause, select a control, and define a test for that control.

content_blocks.title: Safe reference example: XML External Entity and XML Security
content_blocks.code:
XML parser hardening checklist:
- Disable external entity and unsafe DTD processing.
- Do not fetch entities from files or network locations.
- Enforce document size and nesting limits.
- Validate the resulting data against an expected schema.
content_blocks.expected_output: Untrusted XML is parsed without granting the document implicit file or network access.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Parser flags differ by library. Confirm the exact secure configuration in the parser’s official documentation and test it locally.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Use a clean local test account and synthetic data. Reset the test fixture after recording the result; do not include credentials or private data in the course report.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake and recovery
content_blocks.text: Do not confuse an observation with proof or rely on a UI-only restriction. Treat external input and identity claims as untrusted until validated, enforce the control on the server, and cover expected and denied behavior with regression tests. If evidence is ambiguous, reduce the test to one condition, inspect the application code/configuration, and repeat only within the permitted scope.

content_blocks.title: Execution and safety boundary
content_blocks.text: The current CodeLeaf playground is an HTML/CSS/JavaScript preview, not a secure runner for arbitrary server code. This example is a static reference unless the run instructions explicitly identify a supported local environment. Use a private local lab or a test system with written authorization; do not test unrelated public systems.
